findings.claim: TidyFindings reports every removed go.mod line as a requirement the head no longer needs, even when the same diff re-adds that module. A requirement that tidy only moves or rewrites is a false T2 finding. This happens in the case that triggers the check: a commit removes the last direct import of a module that another dependency still needs. Tidy then rewrites `-\tx v1.2.3` as `+\tx v1.2.3 // indirect`, and the sweep fires `T2 go-mod-tidy <dir>: go.mod: require x v1.2.3`. A version bump (`-x v1.2.3` / `+x v1.3.0`) and the reverse change from indirect to direct are reported the same way. The sweep records `fired`, which makes the sweeper answer a candidate that is not real. The docs and the CHANGELOG call a finding a module the head no longer needs.
evidence: The loop at sweep.go:509-517 keeps any `-` line inside a go.mod section whose fields are `<path> v<ver>`. It never looks for the same path on a `+` line.
The only test (sweep_test.go:561-585) adds a different module on the `+` side (`golang.org/x/new`), so the move and bump cases are not covered.
I read this from the diff and did not run it. Whether tidy moves an entry to the indirect block depends on go's behaviour, which I did not check.
